title: Accelerating U-Net: A Patchwise Memory Optimization Approach for Image Segmentation
problem: U-Net models achieve exceptional segmentation performance but require enormous memory for training due to skip connections and large intermediate feature maps. This limits deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Image segmentation is critical for medical imaging, autonomous systems, and edge AI. Reducing memory overhead while maintaining model accuracy enables practical deployment on embedded hardware.
method: Patchwise image segmentation strategy converting full images into smaller patches to reduce memory footprint. Unified architecture supporting both Standard Convolution (SCONV) and Transpose Convolution (TCONV) operations. Quantization applied to further reduce memory consumption. Extensive experiments on resource-constrained hardware.
key_novelty: Patch-based memory optimization targeting skip connections in U-Net, combined with unified SCONV/TCONV architecture and quantization for edge deployment.
contributions: Patchifying technique reducing memory overhead while maintaining IoU (Intersection Over Union)
Unified SCONV/TCONV architecture eliminating separate convolution paths
Improved both memory efficiency and IoU metrics
Practical edge device implementation demonstrating feasibility
limitations: Quantitative memory and IoU improvements not specified in abstract
Limited dataset evaluation; generalization to diverse segmentation tasks unclear
Patch size selection and optimal configuration not discussed
No comparison with other model compression techniques (pruning, distillation)
Edge device specifications and performance metrics not provided
Inference latency and throughput not mentioned
